 Micron Technology (MU) Rides AI Memory Optimism, Is The 51% Discount View Credible?
 October 29, 2026 SI Simply Wall St Micron Technology (MU) is back in focus after investors received fresh detail on its upcoming US$0.15 cash dividend, associated with an October 14, 2026 ex dividend date that anchors the latest move in the stock.
 Recent trading in Micron Technology has been choppy, with a 1 day share price return of 5.9% and a 7 day share price gain of 7.6% partially clawing back a 30 day share price decline of 6.7%. The very large 1 year total shareholder return of 334.3% and roughly 13x 3 year total shareholder return point to momentum that is still firmly intact, even as investors reassess AI driven memory demand and risk after a sharp run up.
 Scan Micron Technology's peers riding the same AI memory theme by running through our hand picked 54 AI infrastructure stocks for context on where sentiment and capital are concentrating.
 Micron Technology’s surge, pullback, and fresh dividend news all sit at the crossroads of strong AI memory demand and a changing mood in the market. How much of today’s price really reflects the underlying business rather than sentiment swings?
 Advertisement Most Popular Narrative: 51% Undervalued
 On the most widely followed narrative for Micron Technology, the fair value sits at $2,018.05 compared with a last close of $983.23. This frames the recent pullback against a much higher long run valuation anchor.
 Micron’s long-term profitability has shifted from a volume-driven commodity model to a value-driven enterprise model. The company''s primary profit pools are concentrated in its high-margin server, enterprise cloud, and data center memory divisions. By prioritizing fabrication capacity for advanced server DDR5, high-capacity solid-state storage, and specialized HBM3E modules, Micron can leverage its operating structures to achieve consolidated gross margins exceeding 70% during tight market cycles. This helps isolate its financial performance from historical client PC volatility. 
 See why 133 investors see Micron Technology as 51% undervalued .
 Result: Fair Value of $2,018.05 (UNDERVALUED) 
 Still, that 51% discount view on Micron Technology collides with two obvious swing factors: HBM4 execution risk and rising Chinese capacity in mainstream memory.
 Find out about the key risks to this Micron Technology narrative .
 Another take on Micron Technology’s valuation
 The narrative fair value pins Micron Technology at $2,018.05, roughly 51% above the recent $983.23 share price. Our DCF model paints a cooler picture, with a future cash flow value of $851, which sits below today’s level. That split raises a simple question: Which set of assumptions do you trust more?
